key_insight: Foundation interatomic potentials capture metallic-glass disorder most reliably when pre-training includes liquid and amorphous configurations, with target-specific fine-tuning adding only modest gains.
engineering_relevance: Well-validated foundation potentials could reduce reliance on composition-specific models and costly ab initio simulations when predicting metallic-glass structure and properties.
method: Benchmark MACE foundation models against EAM during Cu-Zr-Al molecular dynamics quenches.
Validate against DFT and experiment at Cu46Zr46Al8 and across the ternary’s good glass-forming region.
Compare fine-tuning on surrogate-generated glass structures with specialization on ASSYST-generated small periodic cells.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that models pre-trained with non-equilibrium data, such as OMAT, outperform composition-specific EAM and reproduce structural, quenching, elastic, mechanical and thermal behavior at near first-principles accuracy.
watch_item: Transferability beyond the tested Cu-Zr-Al region remains unestablished, and specialization on small crystalline cells can degrade disorder predictions.
paper_title: Foundation interatomic potentials capture structural disorder in metallic glasses
